name: Performance-Explainability Framework for Multivariate Time Series
description: Our research aims to propose a new performance-explainability analytical framework to assess and benchmark machine learning methods. The framework details a set of characteristics that systematize the performance-explainability assessment of existing machine learning methods. In order to illustrate the use of the framework, we apply it to benchmark the current state-of-the-art multivariate time series classifiers.
reputation: Academic research contribution illustrating a performance–explainability framework for multivariate time series; of niche adoption in the time-series research community but not a broadly used standard benchmark.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on multivariate time-series classifiers; dataset/task difficulty and metrics vary across problems, so results are heterogeneous; small/dataset-specific effects can dominate comparisons.
